published_statement: Mars-Senovilla, verbatim (preprint pp.3, 7-9). Definition, p.3: 'A space-time, V4, has axial symmetry if there is an effective realization of the one-dimensional torus T into V4 that is an isometry and such that its set of fixed points constitutes a two-dimensional surface.' Property 3, p.7-8: 'But if we now choose the standard parametrization for the torus such that phi goes from 0 to 2 pi, then we have that d tau_2pi |_Q = Id |_Q. In consequence, and given that the realization is effective, we have a = 1 as required.' Property 5, p.8: 'At the axis of symmetry we have [grad_rho(sigma^2) grad^rho(sigma^2)] / (4 sigma^2) --> 1. This is the popular regularity condition of the axis of symmetry, which usually is assumed to assure the standard 2 pi-periodicity of phi. We will prove this result by using the projector H_ab constructed above.' (the text layer prints the fraction as 'grad_rho(~sigma2) grad 4~sigma2 rho(~sigma2) --> 1'; restored to the standard form, which reaudit M1 evaluates.) End of Sec. 2, p.8-9: 'The last expression shows that the norm ~sigma2 |x coincides, at first non-trivial order, with this distance from x to the axis of symmetry. If we now consider the orbit of the axial symmetry which passes through x we have that its length is 2 pi ~sigma2 |x, because the norm of a Killing vector field remains constant alongs its orbits. Then we have found that the length of the axial orbit is, at first relevant order, 2 pi times the distance from x to the axis of symmetry, which states what is ususally called elementary flatness.' Scope, abstract p.1: 'The results are completely general and do not depend on Einstein's equations or any particular matter content.'
published_hypotheses: READ (p.3): an EFFECTIVE isometric action of the 1-torus whose fixed-point set is a 2-surface (the axis), inside a spacetime V4 that is a manifold with a metric at the axis (the proof expands sigma and H_ab in a coordinate system at axis points, p.8: 'sigma_mu(x) = (x^nu - Q^nu) grad_nu sigma_mu |_Q + o(2)').
READ (p.7-8): the torus is given 'the standard parametrization ... such that phi goes from 0 to 2 pi'; with effectiveness this forces the tangent-space rotation rate a = 1.

READ (p.8): the condition is proved as a PROPERTY of such a spacetime ('We will prove this result'), and named 'the popular regularity condition of the axis of symmetry'. The direction is regular axis => elementary flatness; M&S do not claim the converse.
READ (abstract p.1): no field equations and no matter content are used.
hypothesis_drift: CONFIRMED FROM THE SOURCE (was computed only in the first audit): the 2 pi period. M&S p.7-8 obtain the condition only after choosing 'the standard parametrization for the torus such that phi goes from 0 to 2 pi', and p.8 says the condition 'usually is assumed to assure the standard 2 pi-periodicity of phi'. axial.py:33 writes 'W^2 dphi^2' and axial.py:186 'regular axis: W(0) = 0 and W'(0) = 1' with no period. Under period 2 pi k the normalised condition is k W'(0) = 1 (reaudit M2). This is a convention a reader will almost always supply, but the source states it and the tree does not.

SHARPENED BY THE SOURCE: the axis end of the boundary term. axial.py:43-45 'A REGULAR AXIS gives W(0) = 0 and W'(0) = 1 ... Both boundary terms vanish' needs W Psi' -> 0 at r = 0, which elementary flatness does not control. What M&S call a regular axis is more than elementary flatness: a smooth effective torus action with a 2-surface of fixed points in a manifold. COMPUTED here (reaudit M4; this is NOT a statement in M&S): under that smoothness every axially invariant metric function, g_zz = e^{2 Psi} included, is a smooth function of r^2, so Psi' = O(r) and W Psi' -> 0. So the owner's prose ('A REGULAR AXIS gives ... Both boundary terms vanish') is RIGHT if 'regular axis' is read as M&S's regular axis. But the owner's HYPOTHESES[0] (axial.py:186), which specthm.py:606-608 carries as H_axial, reduces regularity to W(0) = 0 and W'(0) = 1, and that alone does not give the axis term: Psi = a log(r/(1+r)) keeps W'(0) = 1 with W Psi' -> a (M4). The narrowing is between the owner's prose and the owner's hypothesis tuple, and the source supplies the stronger reading.

WITHDRAWN (first audit's 'WEAKENED NAME'): the first audit said the tree's label 'regular axis' claims too much because elementary flatness is necessary but not sufficient for regularity. M&S themselves name the condition 'the popular regularity condition of the axis of symmetry' (p.8) and prove it as a consequence of regularity. The tree's name follows the source's usage. The logical point (necessary, not sufficient) stands and agrees with M&S's direction of proof, but it is not a drift from the source and should not be counted as one.
ORIENTATION (unchanged): Property 5 gives W'(0)^2 = 1 (reaudit M1); W'(0) = +1 follows from W > 0 off the axis.

lacked_data: M's hypothesis does not bite: M&S (READ, abstract) derive the condition without field equations or matter content, and the owner's use carries no datum. What is missing is on the tree's side: the 2 pi period (stated by M&S p.7-8, absent from axial.py:33, 186) and the axis-end condition W Psi' -> 0 (supplied by M&S's smooth-axis hypotheses, per reaudit M4, but not by the owner's HYPOTHESES[0]). Neither changes O4's sign: the conical term is period-invariant and, without the axis condition, the weighted energy goes to -inf rather than turning positive (first audit D2, E1).

grade_evidence: READ, Mars-Senovilla (gr-qc/0201045v1) p.8: 'At the axis of symmetry we have [grad(sigma^2)]^2/(4 sigma^2) --> 1. This is the popular regularity condition of the axis of symmetry, which usually is assumed to assure the standard 2 pi-periodicity of phi', proved from 'the standard parametrization for the torus such that phi goes from 0 to 2 pi' and effectiveness (p.7-8: 'we have a = 1 as required'). For the owner's metric this is exactly W(0) = 0, W'(0) = 1 in the Lambda = 0 gauge (reaudit M1-M3, 15/15 PASS), so the owner's condition agrees with the source. The grade stays NARROWED, not STANDS, because the tree uses the condition on a larger class than the source proves it for. (i) The period 2 pi, a stated hypothesis of the source, is absent from axial.py:33 and 186. (ii) axial.py:43-45 infers from 'a regular axis' that the axis boundary term W Psi' vanishes. That holds for M&S's smooth axis (reaudit M4, my derivation, not M&S's text), but the tree's operative HYPOTHESES[0] (axial.py:186, carried into specthm H_axial at specthm.py:606-608) keeps only W(0) = 0 and W'(0) = 1, which does not imply it. Neither gap changes a downstream verdict (first audit D2, E1/E2): O4, R2 and K4 stand as far as this item goes.
